subject: Surge rate stabilizer & conditional credit accord
messages:
From: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@heliosai.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Cc: Kara Lim <kara@heliosai.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Contract renewal and recent usage spike — options?

Alex,

Quick note: we just closed a major customer pilot and our inference consumption for April jumped ~180% vs baseline. Renewal is up in July and our finance team is worried about the near-term bill volatility.

Can Redwood offer any sort of temporary rate protection or credits to cover the surge window? We'd prefer not to commit to a much larger upfront committed spend right now. Open to a short-term amendment (3–6 months) or a conditional play that gives us a modest price hold if usage exceeds an agreed threshold.

Kara and I can jump on a call this week — ideally something concise we can take to our CFO.

Thanks,
Sandeep Rao
VP, Infrastructure Ops | HeliosAI
(sandeep@heliosai.com)

Attachments: usage-spike-summary-202704.pdf (stub)

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>

Cc: Kara Lim <kara@heliosai.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Contract renewal and recent usage spike — options?

Sandeep — thanks for the context and congrats on the pilot win.

We can do a few pragmatic things that don't require a long-term commit today: a short-term price hold window tied to a usage trigger, together with a one-time operational credit to smooth billing for the immediate surge. I want to align internally on exact sizing and approvals; will come back with a concrete proposal by EOD Tuesday.

If you’re free, I can do a 20-minute call Tuesday at 10am PT to walk Kara and your finance lead through the mechanics.

Best,
Alex Martinez

Redwood Inference

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Contract renewal and recent usage spike — HeliosAI (need approval for conditional credit)

Team — forwarding Helios note. Quick ask: Helios is asking for a short-term (3–6 month) price protection plus a one-time operational credit to cover the April surge. They explicitly do not want to convert to a larger committed tier today.

My suggested structure (draft):
- One-time operational credit: $50,000 (applied to the next invoice)
- Price hold: freeze current per-token rate for 90 days from amendment effective date; extendable to 120 days if they agree to a three-month monitoring clause and a usage-forecast checkpoint
- Surge protection trigger: if monthly consumption > 150% of rolling 3-month baseline, rates capped at a blended uplift of +12% (instead of our standard surge tier) for the remainder of the protection window
- Clause: credits are non-recoupable; change to future commitments may include true-up if they sign a higher commit within 90 days

Approval questions: finance signoff on $50k unilateral credit? Legal to OK the conditional cap language? This is a strategic account — recommend we approve on a one-off basis.

Thanks — Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Contract renewal and recent usage spike — HeliosAI (need approval for conditional credit)

Alex — thanks for the draft. Finance is OK to support up to $60k in one-time credits for strategic motion; prefer structuring it as a contra-invoice credit so it’s clear in reporting. Legal prefers the trigger language to be deterministic: use a defined baseline (avg monthly tokens Oct–Dec) and explicit measurement dates.

A couple of recommended edits:
- Reduce the baseline reference ambiguity (use rolling average Jan–Mar or in-contract baseline)
- Cap the total credit exposure: $60k max (credit + any invoice adjustments)
- Price hold: 90 days standard, but allow extension to 120 days if Helios agrees to a 6-week forecasting checkpoint and share of the forecast for that period

If we land on $50–60k credit and deterministic trigger language, I’m comfortable approving. Ben, anything from renewals ops?

—Marissa

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@heliosai.com>
Cc: Kara Lim <kara@heliosai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T10:27:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: 90-day surge stabilizer + one-time credit (HeliosAI)

Sandeep / Kara — thanks for the quick sync Tuesday. Per our call, attached is a short amendment that implements a 90-day surge stabilizer and a one-time operational credit. Highlights below: 

- One-time contra-invoice credit: $55,000 applied to the next invoice
- Price hold: freeze current per-token rate for 90 days from amendment effective date
- Surge trigger: if any monthly consumption during the 90-day window exceeds 150% of the agreed baseline (rolling Jan–Mar 2027 average), rates will be capped at +12% blended uplift for that month only
- Extension option: if Helios shares a 6-week rolling forecast and agrees to a checkpoint review at day 60, we will extend the hold to 120 days
- Accounting note: credits recorded as contra-revenue; maximum exposure capped at $60k per finance guidance

Attachment: Redwood_Renewal_Offer_Proposal_20270504.pdf (proposal + amendment draft)

If this looks good I can send the DocuSign link and route to Legal for the minor contract exhibit.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0198

From: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@heliosai.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Cc: Kara Lim <kara@heliosai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-05T16:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: 90-day surge stabilizer + one-time credit (HeliosAI)

Alex — thanks, appreciate the speed. The terms look reasonable. Two quick asks before we sign:
1) Can we extend the price hold to 120 days (we can commit to the 6-week rolling forecast you described)?
2) Can the credit be applied across two invoices (35k / 20k) instead of a single invoice to help with cashflow timing on our side?

If you can accept both, I’m happy to move to signature tomorrow.

—Sandeep
